newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BBL FIRM, NO SPECULATION THIS TIME-DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: BBL FIRM, NO SPECULATION THIS TIME-DEALERS.

text.p: Shares in Belgian bank BBL outperformed the Bel-20 share index on Tuesday, rising by 2.6 percent, but dealers were reluctant to blame fresh takeover speculation for the interest in the bank stock.
BBL was up 230 francs at 9,180 in early afternoon trade, while the Bel-20 gained 1.28 percent at 2,451.53 points, partly on the back of gains by the financial sector as a whole.
"At around 9,000 francs the share is a 'buy' as a multi-year investment (irrespective of changes in core BBL shareholders)," bi-weekly investor magazine Swingtrend said.

"BBL was good yesterday...that trend is continuing today," a trader said, adding the share, as well as the whole of the financial sector, benefited from news that the German Bundesbank was holding its key repo rate steady for now.
"There is a buyer in the market," said another trader, noting that at about 4,400 shares traded volume was "not exaggerated." He gave no details.
A third said, "There is no news on BBL as such. I doubt it is takeover speculation. The share is just being bought at the lower levels."
The share fell at the end of July from a year high of 9,930 francs to 9,070 on August 4. After a few days of consolidation it slipped to a low of 8,950 on August 11.

On a longer-term view BBL had gained a solid 50 percent since the start of the year. In that context the 10 percent end-July correction fitted in with a 10 percent fall seen in March and an eight percent drop recorded in June, both followed by fresh buying.
"It is a correction," a fourth trader said of Tuesday's buying, adding there were "serious buyers" in the market.
Meanwhile, BBL remains the object of rumours.
Swingtrend said speculation about increased chances of a takeover of BBL in the wake of the merger of shareholder Winterthur and Swiss compatriot Credit Suisse could push BBL stock higher.
"(That) is an argument not to sell BBL shares now. Otherwise, we advise not to speculate in the short term," the magazine said.
Winterthur has about eight percent in BBL and has been cited as a buyer of Belgian insurer Royale Belge.
It has formally denied it is interested.
Should the Swiss insurer nevertheless snap up its Belgian fellow, it would hold hold more than a fifth of BBL. Royale Belge has a 12.4 percent equity stake in BBL.
Royale Belge has been the subject of sale speculation since the merger of insurer UAP with AXA. Via an investment vehicle the merged French group owns 51.2 percent of Royale Belge.
Shares in Royale Belge lagged the Bel-20 on Tuesday, trading up 0.96 percent at 10,550 francs.
